title: astra.registry.alert/1
description:
state/alerts/<fingerprint>.json — TRUST-14's alert record: one per fingerprint, written by the service path's publish job in the run whose alert the channel reported delivered, and the record TRUST-32's gate reads (contract B.4 from 2.4.0; registry plan TRUST-14, TRUST-32, B-T3.3b).

REGISTRY-ONLY. No other party reads it, so it is outside SCOPE-8's two-way test and SCOPE-7's file. It is inside TRUST-31's set, as its fourteenth schema, because tools/validate.mjs judges every record against it by literal path from this repository, and a writer who could edit it from outside the set could make the publish path's first check pass a record TRUST-32 reads.

EXACTLY SIX MEMBERS, and they are bot/lib/service-publish.mjs's ALERT_MEMBERS and alertProblems, rule for rule: bot/tests/service.test.mjs holds the two to one verdict on every case it builds, so a rule added to one and not the other is red.

fingerprint.$comment: The submission fingerprint the alert was raised for, 16 lowercase hex. The file is named for it.

event.$comment: TRUST-14's event: an approval, which since contract 3.0.0 exists only for a change-of-hands hold (DEC-6; DEC-19). Until 3.0.0 a second event, `delay_elapsed`, recorded a delayed fingerprint past its publish_after; the service path no longer delays anything, no such record was ever committed, and one would name an event TRUST-14 no longer raises.

delivered_at.$comment: The message time the channel reported (§0.7). TRUST-32 publishes nothing before it exists, so no record is written without it.
